black-d01.inserted: Had _Black_ stayed the beta product it was before 2022, that note could not be made: any release, even a patch release, would have been free to reshuffle your code.

black-d04.inserted: If some of your developers are still on Python 3.9, and so pinned to a _Black_ from before 25.12.0 (when runtime support for 3.9 was removed), nothing here changes for them: these settings describe isort's output, not the interpreter _Black_ runs on.

black-d05.inserted: _Black_ formats Python 3 source only; the ability to format Python 2 code was removed in 22.0.

black-d06.inserted: For a module that still has to parse as Python 2 — `print` statements, `except Error, e:` — pass `-t py27` so _Black_ picks the matching grammar.

black-d07.inserted: Because the server pulls in `aiohttp`, give it a virtualenv of its own: `python3.9 -m venv blackd-env`, then `blackd-env/bin/pip install 'black[d]'`.

black-d08.inserted: If your test suite stores formatted snapshots, expect a handful of them to start failing the first time you run a newly upgraded _Black_, and plan to regenerate them as part of every version bump.

click-d01.inserted: Spell the optional parameters of that override as `t.Optional[click.Context]` rather than `click.Context | None`: the `|` form is not evaluated at runtime on every interpreter Click still runs on.

click-d02.inserted: Were {class}`MultiCommand` still the base class behind every group, chaining would have to be re-implemented by each subclass that wanted it.

click-d03.inserted: On Python 3.8 and 3.9, upgrade the installer first with `python -m pip install --upgrade pip`, then run the command above again.

click-d04.inserted: If your application still runs on one of those consoles, keep its `colorama.init()` call where it is; Click does not make that call for you.

click-d06.inserted:
Both sessions below were recorded with completion enabled for the command:

```console
$ eval "$(_COPY_COMPLETE=source_bash copy)"
```

click-d07.inserted:
Styled output is captured the same way in both modes. To assert on the escape sequences themselves, undo the translation first and compare the raw output:

```python
import colorama
from click.testing import CliRunner
from myapp import cli


def test_color():
    colorama.deinit()
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cli, color=True)
    assert "\x1b[32m" in result.stdout
```

click-d08.inserted: Click's own completion support covers Bash 4.4 and up, Zsh, Fish and PowerShell; `shtab` in the table above is the option for shells outside that set.

flask-d02.inserted:
If ``recorded`` comes back empty in CI even though the view rendered a
template, check that image for signalling support before looking for a bug
in the fixture.

flask-d03.inserted:
This is also the place for one-time setup such as creating tables, since Flask no
longer has a hook that runs before the first request is handled.

flask-d05.inserted:
The startup output includes the environment the server is running in, so check
that it says ``development`` before you try to reproduce a bug against it.

flask-d06.inserted:
Build the virtualenv with the oldest interpreter you plan to run in
production, for example ``python3.9 -m venv .venv``, so that the
wheels installed into it work on every host you deploy to.

flask-d07.inserted:
If debug mode were still switched on by an environment variable rather than by
the ``--debug`` option, it would be much easier to leave it enabled by accident
on a production host.

flask-d08.inserted:
If you are bringing over an older configuration that decided this by comparing
``app.env`` against ``'production'``, switch the check to ``app.debug`` as shown
above.

httpx-d01.inserted: Had the plain-string form of `verify` not been deprecated, this last example could have been shortened to `httpx.Client(verify="path/to/certs.pem")`.

httpx-d02.inserted: If you are porting settings out of a script that configured a client with a `proxies={...}` mapping, that argument has been removed; these variables, or an explicit `proxy=` or `mounts=`, are what replaces it.

httpx-d03.inserted: Before installing, create and activate a virtual environment for the checkout with `python3.8 -m venv venv` and `source venv/bin/activate`, so that the pinned development dependencies don't end up in your system site-packages.

httpx-d04.inserted: For a quick check of a single route, drop the `transport=` argument, pass `app=app` to the client instead, and request the path exactly as above.

httpx-d05.inserted: If `https://www.example.com/` sends you on somewhere else, `r` is the response from the end of the chain, and `r.history` lists the redirects that were made along the way.

httpx-d06.inserted:
An equivalent configuration, written as a single mapping:

```python
proxies = {
    "http://": "http://localhost:8030",
    "https://": "http://localhost:8031",
}

with httpx.Client(proxies=proxies) as client:
    ...
```

httpx-d08.inserted: * Redirect responses are handed back to you as they are, and are only followed if you ask for it with `follow_redirects=True`.

pip-d02.inserted:
Were PyPI still answering XML-RPC search queries, a list of names like the one
above could have been assembled from `pip search` output instead of being typed
out by hand.

pip-d03.inserted:
That backtracking algorithm is the one every `pip install` runs today; the older
resolver it replaced is deprecated and is not supported.

pip-d04.inserted:
Nothing is left behind for a later run to pick up either: once `pip install .`
finishes, you will not find a `build/` directory or an `.egg-info` sitting next
to your `pyproject.toml`.

pip-d05.inserted:
If the target machine runs a Python old enough that the current pip will not
install on it, build the wheelhouse there with the last pip release that ran on
that interpreter; the requirements file, hashes included, carries over unchanged.

pip-d06.inserted:
The interpreters the test job runs against are listed in the matrix of that
workflow:

.. code-block:: yaml

    strategy:
      matrix:
        python: ["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13", "3.14", "3.15"]

pip-d07.inserted: - Whether the project is on PyPI under the name being used: `pip search <project-name>`

pip-d08.inserted:
If you need the environment working right now, run the install again without
`--use-feature=2020-resolver`, get yourself unblocked, and come back to the
strategies below once you have time to work out the constraints.

poetry-d01.inserted: Had the `shell` command not been moved out into `poetry-plugin-shell`, users who would rather not work inside a nested shell would have had no way to leave that behaviour out of their installation.

poetry-d03.inserted:
If you edit a constraint in `pyproject.toml` by hand, bring the lock file back in sync from the project root:

```bash
poetry lock --no-update
```

poetry-d04.inserted: To work with the tools you have just added, activate the project's environment with `poetry shell` and then call them directly - `pytest`, say - instead of prefixing every invocation with `poetry run`.

poetry-d05.inserted: Note that the Export plugin is no longer installed by default with Poetry 2.0; if you need `poetry export`, add `poetry-plugin-export` to your Poetry installation yourself.

poetry-d06.inserted: If you are working on a machine that still has a Poetry 1.x installation, `poetry shell` is available there without installing anything extra.

poetry-d07.inserted: Some deployment tooling cannot read `poetry.lock` directly. Once `poetry install` has succeeded, write the same pinned set out for it with `poetry export --without-hashes --output requirements.txt`.

poetry-d08.inserted: The environment you activate for this stays in effect until you type `exit`, so leave it again before you run Poetry commands for another project.

pytest-d01.inserted:
.. tab:: setup.cfg

    .. code-block:: ini

        [pytest]
        doctest_optionflags = NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL

pytest-d03.inserted: If your project still keeps its pytest settings in a ``[pytest]`` section of a ``setup.cfg`` file, rename that section to ``[tool:pytest]`` and the option can be set there in the same way.

pytest-d04.inserted: If you need to check your package against more than one interpreter, create one environment per version -- for example ``python3.9 -m venv .venv39`` and ``python3.13 -m venv .venv313`` -- and install ``pytest`` into each of them.

pytest-d05.inserted: ``pytest.yield_fixture`` is nothing but an old alias of :py:func:`@pytest.fixture <pytest.fixture>`: it has been deprecated for a long time and pytest 10 will drop it, so fixtures that yield a value are decorated with ``@pytest.fixture`` too.

pytest-d07.inserted: If the project also has a ``pytest.ini``, that is the file named on the ``configfile:`` line of the run header, so add the ``addopts`` entry there instead.

pytest-d08.inserted: If ``tmp_path`` were not available, the test would have to request the legacy ``tmpdir`` fixture instead and convert the ``py.path.local`` object it hands back with ``Path(str(tmpdir))`` before using any :mod:`pathlib` API on it.

requests-d01.inserted:
If you would rather ask for the credentials than keep them in the source, the
tuple form composes nicely with the standard library::

    >>> import getpass
    >>> username = raw_input('Username: ')
    >>> requests.get('https://httpbin.org/basic-auth/user/pass',
    ...              auth=(username, getpass.getpass()))
    <Response [200]>

requests-d02.inserted: - If your deployment is still on Python 3.9, this is the last release you will be able to upgrade to; support for it ends in the next feature release.

requests-d03.inserted: Hard-coding ``'utf-8'`` keeps that decision in your hands. If you would rather let the detector pick, pin ``chardet`` in your requirements file next to Requests -- a different release of it can put a different label on the same bytes, and ``r.encoding`` follows whatever your resolver installed.

requests-d04.inserted: When the headers name no charset at all, the guess is made from the body instead: that job goes to ``charset-normalizer``, unless you already have ``chardet`` installed (or asked for it with the ``use_chardet_on_py3`` extra), in which case Requests uses ``chardet``.

requests-d06.inserted: Had Requests still needed to run on interpreters older than 3.10, these annotations would have had to spell every union as `typing.Optional`; as it is, they use PEP 604 syntax throughout.

requests-d07.inserted: Keep the snippets themselves conservative as well: a ``match`` statement or an ``int | None`` annotation will not even parse on the oldest interpreter Requests still supports, so reach for ``if``/``elif`` and ``typing.Optional`` instead.

requests-d08.inserted: Not installed yet? Run ``$ pipenv install requests`` in your project directory first -- it will add the dependency to your Pipfile -- and then try the snippet above.
